A city. Your team. A new beginning.
Bakers on the way to pick up butter
The machines are still there. What we lacked were honest delivery plans and people who keep their promises.
Between the warm rocks, our next harvest is growing. The old farm is finally getting reliable buyers again.
Let's fill the shelves and trust together again.
Burning Hills has shown what we can achieve together. Now Big Rock City gets its own chance.
All six residents combine their experiences: open books, reliable technology, good food, music and green paths. The new quarry festival belongs to the city and its people.
Big Rock City came together to carry out this project. Everyone involved remains part of the town, with their own stories.

The residents plan and decide together.
Rocko: Samira never brought in the chairs outside the café. Repair the town warehouse and café. The government can replace missing starting funds, but we must earn trust ourselves.
Nothing's been happening in the city for a while. A reliable warehouse and our first coffee shop are bringing life back to the streets.
The first meeting spot is set up! Finally, people in the neighborhood can gather again somewhere.
Rocko: Assign teams to the warehouse and café, then sell the first cup. Soon the residents will tell you how they kept the town going through the difficult times.
Do you hear that? People are coming back to the neighborhood. When the warehouse delivers and the shop is stocked, we can finally offer them something.
Our first guests are taken care of. It's nice to see the streets come alive again.
Nia: Assign a warehouse manager and driver. Once the first delivery arrives and the farm runs automatically, we'll open the routes into Copper Lane.
Our team is ready. I'm organizing the warehouse, drivers bring goods further. As soon as the farm runs, we'll turn individual workshops into a real cooperative.
The first delivery has arrived! I'm proud of the drivers. That's how our farm will become a cooperative.
One delivery instead of a speech
Nia: There are still unpaid delivery notes hanging in the warehouse. Repair the building. Then we'll replace empty promises with goods that actually arrive.
I'm Nia. When goods arrive on time, you hardly notice how much planning is behind it. Our warehouse will connect the farm to the city.
The warehouse is ready. Now our goods have a safe place and our team has a shared hub.
Rocko: The mayor has vanished, but the people stayed. Talk to Mila at the farm. We'll start with what is still here.
Hey! I'm Mila. Nice to have you on board. Here the first plants are growing for our new start. I'd be happy to show you how we care for them.
Great to have met you! I think we'll make a great team. Our new start can begin!
Mila: The soil is good; the farm simply stopped working. Repair the first growing plot. A working start means more than another promise.
This place has potential. If we fix it up again, the first harvest will grow here soon. I've already got the seedlings ready.
Hey, our first cultivation plot is thriving again! The seedlings have a home. I'm already looking forward to the first harvest.
Rocko: Collect the market's first daily yield. Supplies now flow reliably. The books remain open, and the residents shape their next chapters themselves.
You've turned the first workshops into a functioning city. I'm proud of our team. Soon you'll be able to choose your own path.
We've made it. The city is standing on its own feet again. Thanks for believing in our team.
A new beginning belongs to all
Mila: Our new helper wants to know where he's needed. Assign him to the field so we can keep working reliably while you visit Burning Hills.
I'll stay here and take care of the cultivation. If you put me in charge, I'll keep the plants in shape while you're taking care of the town.
I've taken over here. The plants are in good hands with me, and you can rely on me.
Rocko: Enno's old machines can do more than stand idle. Repair the butter works, market and bakery so Big Rock City can support itself again.
With the butter factory, supermarket, and bakery, we can close the next big gap. The aroma of fresh bread will draw in the whole city.
The workshops are standing. The bakery alone is already smelling like a good morning for our city.
The industrial district is getting a task
Rocko: Staff the three businesses and send off the first butter and pastries. Everyday life should return to the warm Rock Steps.
Now everything fits together: the factory delivers butter, the baker picks it up and makes something good out of it. That's exactly how I imagined our city.
Our baked goods are a hit with the people! From cultivation to the counter, everyone is now contributing their part.
From the old quarry to the table
Mila: This harvest belongs to the town, not a locked safe. Collect the first crate; after that, someone will help you permanently in the field.
The buds are ripe! I love this moment. Let's bring them in, then the next plants will have space.
The first harvest is safely stored away. Well done! You have a knack for plants.
Jaro: The processing facility was never fully set up. Talk to me and repair it. We'll get the old equipment working again.
Jaro is the name. These machines have seen better days, but we'll get them running again. We're refining Mila's harvest here into high-quality buds.
The machines are running again! I knew we could get this workshop up and running together.
Jaro: A repaired facility isn't enough. Give the processing team a permanent workplace and a routine the drivers can rely on.
The workshop is running again! I'll take over processing. Regular harvests and a free buffer are all I need for a good workday.
Everything's set up. I'm keeping the processing going – our team will get reliable good stuff.
Rocko: Berta wants real neighbourhoods, not a backdrop for the next election. Choose at least one house and one park on the building plots, then develop them.
A city is more than its workshops. People need a home and a green space to breathe. I'm especially looking forward to that.
The first new homes and park are here. I can already imagine how the neighbors will live together here.
Rocko: Collect the first daily yields, staff the house and park, and complete one resident assignment from the daily tasks. Then we'll head to the works district together.
Our neighborhood is coming alive. Our neighbors support us with daily bonuses, and new connections are forming in the park. Let's take good care of them.
Our neighbors are helping us, and we're helping them. It finally feels like a community again.
The city is counting its people
Rocko: No one sits behind closed doors at the town hall now. Visit it and recruit a team member. Everyone should be able to see the new decisions.
We need more helping hands. In the team, you can get to know someone with a Worker card. I'll take care of making sure everyone finds their right spot.
Our team is growing. New faces, new ideas – that's exactly what the city needs now.
The town hall without secret doors

Berta: We're one step further. Here's something we've accomplished together.

Samira's grandfather opened the café at the old quarry. When city hall collapsed, she still set out chairs every morning. For her, a new beginning starts with a warm cup and an empty seat.
Samira shows you the empty spot in front of her café. She wants reliable guests, not a fancy photo shoot. Get the first small round going.
Samira: We're one step further. There's something we've accomplished together.
